title: fix(sse): ensure correct chunking/framing for partial JSON and delimiter ordering in streaming API
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Fixes incorrect SSE framing that could emit delimiters out-of-order and produce partial/invalid JSON events for streaming responses.
- Improves robustness of OpenAI-compat streaming layer to assemble partial JSON tokens and preserve event ordering.
- Adds unit and integration tests for streaming framing and partial JSON assembly.
description:
Context and motivation:
Streaming responses over SSE have been intermittently producing invalid JSON for downstream consumers (notably OpenAI-compatible clients) when model tokenization produces JSON fragments that split across chunk boundaries. We also observed delimiter ordering issues where final delimiter events (e.g. [DONE] / event terminators) were emitted before the last JSON chunk had been assembled, which caused some clients to stop parsing early.

What this PR changes:
- Introduces a lightweight stateful assembler in redwood/api/sse.py that maintains partial-token buffers per-stream and only emits 'data:' events when a complete event payload or safe delimiter boundary is available. This prevents emitting truncated JSON blobs.
- Adjusts event ordering semantics in redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py so that function/tool-calling and structured output events are emitted atomically (metadata line + payload lines) and the final stream terminator is emitted after flushing any buffered partial JSON.
- Adds strict delimiter handling to avoid double-delimiter emission when upstream layers already include an end marker. We now normalize delimiters at the SSE boundary.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests and an e2e streaming test using the python client and curl to validate real-world parsing behavior.

Checklist:
- [x] Add stateful assembler for partial JSON chunks
- [x] Preserve event ordering for metadata/payload pairs
- [x] Normalize delimiters at the SSE boundary
- [x] Add unit and integration tests
- [x] Run lint/format and CI

Files changed (high level):
- redwood/api/sse.py: new assembler and framing fixes (main logic)
- redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py: ordering + delimiter normalization
- redwood/console/observability/stream_logs.py: minor tracing hooks to help debug ordering regressions
- tests/streaming/test_partial_json_assembly.py: new unit tests covering split tokens and edge cases
- integration_tests/e2e/test_sse_curl_streaming.sh: e2e validation (runs in CI with a small model)
- docs/openai_compat.md: notes about stable streaming semantics and migration guidance

Commits:
- "sse: add partial-json assembler and framing normalization"
- "openai-compat: reorder metadata/payload emission to be atomic"
- "tests: add unit + e2e tests for SSE partial JSON and delimiter ordering"

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): "Core idea looks good. Please ensure the assembler has clear limits to avoid unbounded buffering in adversarial streams."
- Asha Patel (author): "Added a configurable per-stream max-buffer-size and a fast-fail path that emits an error-event if the buffer exceeds the threshold. Added docs note about backpressure."
- Evelyn Zhao (reviewer): "Found a linting nit and asked to add a small comment explaining why we normalize delimiters at the boundary."
- Asha Patel: "Addressed nit and added comment + unit test for double-delimiter input."
- Liam O'Connor (approver): "Verified e2e test run locally; approving pending CI green."

CI summary:
- build: pass
- unit-tests: pass (new streaming unit tests included)
- integration-e2e (docker): pass
- lint/format: initially failed (line-wrap), fixes pushed, final status: pass

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-23 after approvals and green CI. Merge commit: "squash: fix(sse): ensure correct chunking/framing for partial JSON and delimiter ordering in streaming API"

Usage notes / migration guidance:
- No API surface changes for users. Streaming semantics are now more conservative: some consumers that previously tolerated truncated events will see errors instead of silent truncation (this is by design).
- Customers using custom SSE clients should ensure they accept the normalized delimiter semantics described in docs/openai_compat.md.

- Linked ENG-9843: intermittent invalid JSON in OpenAI-compat streaming clients
- Linked ENG-9901: production incident on 2026-02-10 where a Canary service failed to parse structured output during load testing

notes: This change targets streaming stability for the hosted API and the OpenAI compatibility layer. It was prioritized after a Canary regression; the fix is conservative and includes a fast-fail on overly-large partial buffers to avoid resource exhaustion. Observability hooks were added to surface parse errors in the console.
security_considerations: Added a fast-fail to prevent unbounded per-stream buffering; reviewers validated no new injection vector introduced by assembler (we only re-order and buffer tokens, not interpret them).
